resources.string: Added by FairEmail Plus. They only send anything when you use them.
Send from your addy.io aliases, and get stopped before an email shows your real address.
Create one under Settings → API Keys on addy.io. It\'s kept on this phone only, apart from FairEmail\'s settings, so it isn\'t in exports, logs or debug info. Use one you can revoke.
Only change this if you host addy.io yourself.
Stops a send if it would show your real address, and says why. The email stays on your phone: only an alias that needs confirming as yours is looked up on addy.io.
Also warn when an email doesn\'t go through an alias
Asks before any email goes out from your real address. It needs an API key.
Addresses or domains, one per line. Only the warning above skips them.
Name, or leave empty for random

Put the domains an alias is for in its description on addy.io, like \"main account 1password.com\". New mail to it from anywhere else gets a warning, as it may be fake, or the alias was leaked. Tap the warning\'s icon to expect that sender, or to turn the alias off.
Suggest a sender for aliases without one
Mail to an alias whose description names no domain gets a note offering to expect its sender, so you needn\'t edit every description by hand.
Fix, improve, shorten, change the tone of or translate what you write, with OpenAI or Claude and your own API key.
Share large files as links instead of attachments, end-to-end encrypted, with your Gokapi server.
Share a file as a link
Your Gokapi server\'s address. It must be https.

In Gokapi, under API keys, create one that may upload, and nothing else. To have a file deleted when you tap Undo, let it delete files too. It\'s kept on this phone only, apart from FairEmail\'s settings, so it isn\'t in exports, logs or debug info.

The key Gokapi gave you when you set up end-to-end encryption, 44 characters ending in =. If you didn\'t keep it, open Gokapi\'s upload page in the browser you set it up in, and run localStorage.getItem(\"e2ekey\") in its developer console. It never leaves this phone.
Until either runs out, whichever comes first. Then the server deletes the file. You can change it for each file you share.
Every few hours, when you open the app, asks GitHub whether this fork has a newer release, and shows a notification if it has. Long-press About in the side menu to check now.
